The two cards assign composition and community grades to forty fictional sites. A site can have higher
reported need on one measure and lower reported need on the other. The grid and pair view count sites and
comparisons from the saved grades. The risk and joint-event summaries come from the original analysis.


## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Primary saved card.** Composition S has no disclosed comparisons, so its error proportion is not defined.
  Community C discloses 500 pairs. All forty sites occupy three profile cells.
- **Wider-threshold saved card.** With threshold 1/10, S discloses 300 pairs and C discloses 500. Their union
  contains 548 distinct pairs, including 16 with crossed directions. Five of six profile cells are occupied.
- **Crossed site profiles.** In the wider card, S11 has grades (1,2) and S18 has (2,1). S11 has higher reported
  composition priority, and S18 has higher reported community priority. The grades report those priorities separately.
- **Composition comparison withheld.** In the primary card, S11 and S18 share composition grade 1.
  Their composition direction is withheld, while community grades 2 and 1 give S18 higher community priority.
- **An empty profile cell.** In the wider card, zero sites have community grade 3 and composition grade 1.
  The grid shows that combination alongside the occupied cells.

At the primary threshold of 1/20, 25 errors among 500 stated comparisons reach the threshold and 26 exceed it.
The original analysis estimated a zero probability of exceeding the threshold in either domain. It also found
at least one error in 1,871 of 8,000 selection states. The saved output does not include expected error
fractions for domains that state comparisons.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
The original fictional analysis used chains 1–2 to select the reports and chains 3–4 for diagnostics.
Using separate chains for those tasks does not establish independence or verify the intended posterior.
The saved grades let the browser count comparisons, and the saved summaries describe errors in the
original analysis. The joint states needed to rerun the selection or diagnostics are unavailable.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="In postrank"}
The [R script](../../data/recipes/fictional-site-profiles.R) reads the saved grades and summaries with
postrank 1.2.0 and jsonlite. It reproduces the grid and pair directions from those grades.

```r
source("fictional-site-profiles.R")
result <- fictional_site_profiles()
result$summary
```
:::
